name: Kon Tum coffee
summary: Highland coffee dripped slowly through a phin, often over condensed milk and ice as cà phê sữa đá. Some sources call the local bean Robusta and others arabica, and Măng Đen’s cup is light with a mild sour finish.
origin: Kon Tum sits in the coffee belt of the Central Highlands. Dak Ha, just north of downtown, grows over 9,000 hectares of it.
howToEat: Order cà phê sữa đá and let it drip through the phin. The café is where people meet, so stay a while. Many also pour juices and some serve meals.
Go in the morning or after the river walk. Some cafés look over the Đăk Bla.
where: City cafés, the Dak Ha coffee belt north of town, and Măng Đen at 1,200 metres.
seoTitle: Kon Tum coffee — phin drip over ice
seoDescription: Highland coffee dripped through a phin over condensed milk and ice, in cafés over the Đăk Bla and on the Dak Ha coffee belt.
priceBand: 25,000–40,000 VND a cup in town, 200,000–400,000 VND a kilogram of roasted ground beans (Go Vietnam); 30,000–60,000 VND a cup in Măng Đen (Go Vietnam)
